name: FlexInput Virtual Mouse
notes: Plain-HID virtual relative mouse (FunctionMode 0, no companion). 7-byte report: [buttons(5)+pad(3), X lo, X hi, Y lo, Y hi, wheel, hwheel] -- X/Y are int16 relative mickeys, wheel int8 (vertical), hwheel int8 (Consumer AC Pan, horizontal). No Report ID. No feature reports: 0.15.5 gave both wheels a Resolution Multiplier (x8, PIDs 0xF1E3-0xF1E5; x120 at 0xF1E4) for smooth scrolling, but Windows never sent the SET_FEATURE that turns it on (keymouse_hm watched for it on every launch), so it bought nothing, and it was the only change Windows could see in a release with mouse clicks reported late. Removed; smooth scroll pins round to whole notches. Kernel-level pointer input via mouhid: immune to the user-mode injected-input filters that silently eat SendInput (ASUS Armoury Crate stack / hardened Win11 builds -- the reason this profile exists), and games see it as a real raw-input mouse. Reports are built directly by flexinput-virtual's keymouse_hm and published via HidMaestroDevice::write_raw_input; sub-pixel remainders carry across frames on the writer side. VID 0x1209 (pid.codes space, unregistered PID) -- cosmetic only for a software-enumerated node; deliberately NOT 045E or gamepad-adjacent (see xbox360.json). PID bumped 0xF1E1->0xF1E2 when the report grew 6->7 bytes (added Consumer AC Pan / horizontal wheel) so Windows re-enumerates a fresh device and re-reads the new descriptor instead of serving a cached 6-byte one -- a stale descriptor on the persisted node was the suspected cause of dead mouse buttons after the change. Bumped again for the Resolution Multiplier (0xF1E3 x8, 0xF1E4 x120, 0xF1E5 x8) and to 0xF1E6 when it was removed, the descriptor identical to 0xF1E2's (same reason each time: the stale-node guard must destroy and recreate the persisted node). Created in its OWN device container (ownContainer, SwDeviceCreate under SWD\HIDMAESTRO_KBM), not the PC's: a ROOT-enumerated node sits in the PC's container, so Windows took the virtual keyboard for the built-in one and armed Precision Touchpad typing protection, which dropped every left click (touchpad's and virtual mouse's) while a key was held and for about a second after.
